condition: Private open space at ground level; minimum dimension of 3 metres is stated in the same clause.
source_text:
Private open space at the ground level is to have a minimum area of 16sqm
and minimum dimension of 3m.
review_note: NEW. The clause heading on the page is literally '4.1.3.5 Private open space', inside Part 4.1, whose sub-parts on these pages are dwelling-house and secondary-dwelling controls. 'minimum area of 16sqm' is a requirement, and there is no concession to strand in the condition. 16sqm reads small against Parramatta's 100m2; that is what a dense inner-city LGA states, not an extraction error.

condition: Ground level dwellings only; minimum dimension of 4 metres is stated in the same clause; consolidated area required for all dwelling sizes within a development.
source_text: (a) ground level dwellings: 25sqm with a minimum dimension of 4m; and
review_note: NEW. '(a) ground level dwellings: 25sqm with a minimum dimension of 4m' -- unambiguous, and the general apartment control rather than a precinct one. GRAIN checked: the value is the POS area and the 4m dimension correctly stays in the condition instead of being stored as the value.

condition: Upper level units only; minimum dimension of 2 metres is stated in the same clause; consolidated area required for all dwelling sizes within a development.
source_text: (b) upper level units: 10sqm with a minimum dimension of 2m.
review_note: NEW. '(b) upper level units: 10sqm with a minimum dimension of 2m' -- the same clause's upper-level limb. Ground and upper are genuinely different controls with different numbers, so two rows is right here, unlike the 4.1.6.1(2) restatement above.

condition: APPLIES TO 30% OF ALL BEDROOMS, not every bedroom -- each of that 30% must have access to private open space of at least 4sqm, in the form of a balcony or terrace area.
source_text:
(5) 30% of all bedrooms are to have access to private open space with a
minimum area of 4sqm in the form of a balcony or terrace area.
review_note: NEW, and the qualifier is load-bearing: this is not 4sqm of POS for every boarding house room. The clause requires 30% OF ALL BEDROOMS to have access to at least 4sqm as a balcony or terrace. A consumer reading value_min without that would apply it to every room. Qualifier moved to the front of the condition so it cannot be missed.

condition: Contiguous, provided at ground level, located to the rear of each dwelling; minimum dimension of 6 metres is stated in the same clause; open space within the front setback is excluded from this calculation (C.05 of the same section).
source_text:
A minimum 100m² of private open space must be provided for each dwelling. This space is to
be contiguous, provided at ground level, located to the rear of each dwelling, and have a
minimum dimension of 6 metres.
review_note: NEW. Part 3.3.1, heading 'RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT DWELLING HOUSES, SECONDARY DWELLINGS AND DUAL OCCUPANCIES'. 'A minimum 100m2 of private open space must be provided for each dwelling' -- a requirement, not a target. Contiguity, ground level, rear location and the 6m dimension all correctly stay in the condition rather than displacing the value.

condition: Contiguous, at ground level, located to the rear of each dwelling, with direct access from internal living spaces; minimum dimension of 6 metres is stated in the same clause.
source_text:
A minimum 100m² of private open space must be provided for each dwelling. Private open
space must be contiguous, at ground level, located to the rear of each dwelling, allow direct
access from internal living spaces, and have a minimum dimension of 6 metres.
review_note: NEW. Part 3.3.2, the dual occupancy sub-part. Same 100m2 as the dwelling house control but a separate clause for a separate dev_type, so unlike the terrace/townhouse pair below this is not a duplicate: a consumer querying dual_occupancy would otherwise get nothing.

condition: May be provided as a patio or balcony.
source_text:
A minimum 12m² of private open space must be associated with a secondary dwelling. This may
be provided as a patio or balcony.
review_note: NEW. Part 3.3.3, secondary dwellings. 'A minimum 12m2 of private open space must be associated with a secondary dwelling. This may be provided as a patio or balcony.' The second sentence widens what counts; it does not change the number, so it belongs in the condition where it is.

condition: Townhouses (Section 3.4.1, Multi-Dwelling Housing); contiguous, provided at ground level, located to the rear of each dwelling; minimum dimension of 5 metres is stated in the same clause; open space within the street setback is excluded from this calculation (C.04 of the same section).
source_text:
A minimum 40m² of private open space must be provided for each dwelling. This space is to be
contiguous, provided at ground level, located to the rear of each dwelling, and have a minimum
dimension of 5 metres.
review_note: NEW. Part 3.4.1, 'RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT MULTI-DWELLING HOUSING'. 40m2 per dwelling, contiguous, ground level, rear, minimum dimension 5m. This is Parramatta's general multi-dwelling answer.

condition: Manor houses (Part 3.4.3). Apartments at GROUND level; minimum dimension 2 metres.
source_text:
C.03 For apartments at ground level, a minimum private open space area of 15m² is to be provided
with a minimum dimension of 2 metres.
review_note: dev_type CORRECTED to manor_house. Part 3.4.3 is the manor house sub-part -- page 96, clause 3.4.3.2 C.02, states 'manor houses shall be a maximum of 2-storeys' -- and this clause is 3.4.3.6 on page 100, the same sub-part. Proposed as multi_dwelling_housing it would have contradicted the 40m2 multi_dwelling_housing row from 3.4.1.5, with nothing in dev_type to tell the two apart. section_ref also corrected: a bare 'C.03' cites nothing in a 1,400-page DCP. The part number is used and no sub-number is invented, because the page does not state one. No number changed. Ground-level apartments within a manor house: 15m2.

condition: Manor houses (Part 3.4.3). FIRST-FLOOR level dwellings, 1-bedroom/studio units; minimum dimension 2 metres.
source_text: a) 1-bedroom/studio units must provide a minimum of 8m² per dwelling.
review_note: dev_type CORRECTED to manor_house. Part 3.4.3 is the manor house sub-part -- page 96, clause 3.4.3.2 C.02, states 'manor houses shall be a maximum of 2-storeys' -- and this clause is 3.4.3.6 on page 100, the same sub-part. The part number is used and no sub-number is invented, because the page does not state one. No number changed. First-floor 1-bedroom/studio units: 8m2. The three limbs of C.04 are three different minimums and so are three rows, not one.

condition: Apartment buildings (Part 3.5.1), per dwelling, 1-bedroom/studio units; contiguous area with a minimum dimension of 2 metres.
source_text: a) 1-bedroom/studio units must provide a minimum of 8m² per dwelling.
review_note: NEW, and the section_ref was not usable. Part 3.5.1 is 'RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT APARTMENT BUILDINGS' (page heading 3.5.1.5), so residential_flat_building is right -- but a bare 'C.08' cites nothing in a 1,400-page DCP. Corrected to '3.5.1 C.08': the part is provable from the page, the sub-number is not, so none is invented. No number changed. This is the 1-bedroom/studio limb of a three-limb clause.

condition: ON-SITE MANAGER'S ACCOMMODATION ONLY -- this is not the boarding house's resident POS requirement. Where accommodation is provided for an on-site manager, one area of at least 8m2 with a minimum dimension of 2.5 metres, adjacent to that accommodation and not in the front setback area.
source_text:
C.48 If accommodation is provided for an on-site manager, one area of at least 8m² with a minimum
dimension of 2.5 metres is to be provided adjacent to that accommodation, other than in the
front setback area.
review_note: NEW, but dangerously narrow if served plainly. This is the POS for an ON-SITE MANAGER'S accommodation in a boarding house -- not the POS a boarding house provides for its residents. Parramatta has no general boarding-house POS row, so a consumer asking the obvious question would get 8m2 and be wrong. Qualifier moved to the very front of the condition.
